before.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements through rank four
before.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $q\in R^{\times}$. In $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]) for $n\ge4$ are $$L_1=0,\quad L_2=q^{-1}T_{(1,2)},\quad L_3=q^{-1}T_{(2,3)}+q^{-2}T_{(1,3)},\quad L_4=q^{-1}T_{(3,4)}+q^{-2}T_{(2,4)}+q^{-3}T_{(1,4)},$$ and in general $L_k=\sum_{j<k}q^{j-k}T_{(j,k)}$. For the standard tableau $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3&4\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ of shape $(3,1)$ the contents of the entries $k=1,2,3,4$ are $0,-1,1,2$ ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]), so the diagonal eigenvalues of $L_1,\dots,L_4$ on the Murphy vector $m_t$ are $[0]_q=0$, $[-1]_q=-q^{-1}$, $[1]_q=1$ and $[2]_q=1+q$; the triangular correction terms $\sum_{v\rhd t}a_vm_v$ are present in general ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]) and vanish only in the semisimple range handled by [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]]. At $q=1$ the four elements specialize to the ordinary Jucys-Murphy elements $X_1=0$, $X_2=(1\,2)$, $X_3=(1\,3)+(2\,3)$, $X_4=(1\,4)+(2\,4)+(3\,4)$ and the eigenvalues to $0,-1,1,2$, the standard contents of $t$.
before.strategy: Substitute into the defining sum; the contents are read off the tableau; the $q=1$ specialization uses [[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]] and $[m]_1=m$ for all integers $m$. The correction terms are governed by [[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] and are not asserted to be zero without the hypothesis $e>n$. No choice is used.

after.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements through rank four
after.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $q\in R^{\times}$. In $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]) for $n\ge4$ are $$L_1=0,\quad L_2=q^{-1}T_{(1,2)},\quad L_3=q^{-1}T_{(2,3)}+q^{-2}T_{(1,3)},\quad L_4=q^{-1}T_{(3,4)}+q^{-2}T_{(2,4)}+q^{-3}T_{(1,4)},$$ and in general $L_k=\sum_{j<k}q^{j-k}T_{(j,k)}$. For the standard tableau $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3&4\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ of shape $(3,1)$ the contents of the entries $k=1,2,3,4$ are $0,-1,1,2$ ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]), so the diagonal eigenvalues of $L_1,\dots,L_4$ on the Murphy vector $m_t$ are $[0]_q=0$, $[-1]_q=-q^{-1}$, $[1]_q=1$ and $[2]_q=1+q$; the triangular correction terms $\sum_{v\rhd t}a_vm_v$ are present in general ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]) in the Murphy basis, even in the semisimple range. In the separated range, replacing $m_t$ by the seminormal vector $f_t$ removes these correction terms, as proved in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]]. At $q=1$ the four elements specialize to the ordinary Jucys-Murphy elements $X_1=0$, $X_2=(1\,2)$, $X_3=(1\,3)+(2\,3)$, $X_4=(1\,4)+(2\,4)+(3\,4)$ and the eigenvalues to $0,-1,1,2$, the standard contents of $t$.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A commutative ring $R$, $q\in R^{\times}$, the Hecke algebra $H_{R,q}(S_n)$, the Jucys-Murphy elements and q-contents ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]), the content vector of a standard tableau ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]), and the q=1 specialization $H_{R,1}(S_n)\cong R[S_n]$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]).

[F1] ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]) $L_k=\sum_{j<k}q^{j-k}T_{(j,k)}$; $[m]_q=1+q+\cdots+q^{m-1}$ for $m\ge0$, $[-m]_q=-q^{-m}[m]_q$ for $m>0$, and $[m]_1=m$ for all $m\in\mathbb Z$.

[F2] ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]) $m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_vm_v$ on the Murphy cell module, so the displayed values are the diagonal entries and the correction terms are as stated.



## Verification

1.1 Substitution: in [F1], for $k=1$ the sum is empty, giving $L_1=0$; for $k=2$ it has the single term $q^{1-2}T_{(1,2)}=q^{-1}T_{(1,2)}$; for $k=3$ it has $q^{-1}T_{(2,3)}+q^{-2}T_{(1,3)}$; and for $k=4$ it has $q^{-1}T_{(3,4)}+q^{-2}T_{(2,4)}+q^{-3}T_{(1,4)}$, matching the displayed list. [given, F1]

1.2 Contents: reading the tableau $t$ with rows $(1,3,4)$ and $(2)$, the node of $1$ is $(1,1)$ with content $1-1=0$, the node of $2$ is $(2,1)$ with content $1-2=-1$, the node of $3$ is $(1,2)$ with content $2-1=1$ and the node of $4$ is $(1,3)$ with content $3-1=2$; by definition $[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ is the q-integer of these contents. [given, F1]

2.1 Eigenvalues: by [F1], $[0]_q=0$, $[-1]_q=-q^{-1}[1]_q=-q^{-1}$, $[1]_q=1$ and $[2]_q=1+q$; substituting into the triangularity formula [F2] gives the stated diagonal eigenvalues $0,-1,1,2$ up to the q-powers $-q^{-1},1,1+q$. The correction terms are exactly the sum $\sum_{v\rhd t}a_vm_v$ of [F2] and are not asserted to vanish outside the semisimple range. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2]

3.1 Specialization: setting $q=1$ in the displayed formulas turns $L_k$ into $\sum_{j<k}(j\,k)=X_k$ by the specialization isomorphism of [[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]] and [F1], giving $X_1=0$, $X_2=(1\,2)$, $X_3=(1\,3)+(2\,3)$ and $X_4=(1\,4)+(2\,4)+(3\,4)$; the eigenvalues $[m]_1=m$ become $0,-1,1,2$, the contents of $t$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F1] ∎

before.title: General type-A decomposition numbers remain unsolved
before.statement:
The two preceding constraints on the decomposition matrix of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are real but limited, and neither solves the general problem. (i) Dominance unitriangularity ([[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]) determines only the diagonal entries $d_{\mu\mu}=1$ and the vanishing region $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$; it gives no value for an off-diagonal entry. (ii) The q-Schaper/Jantzen sum formula ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]]) is a virtual radical-layer identity whose coefficients $
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q})-
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q})$ bound the corresponding composition multiplicities from above; it neither determines a general multiplicity nor produces a positive combinatorial rule. Special coefficient regimes and low-rank calculations determine additional entries (canonically based, weight-one, and small-$n$ cases), but the classification of irreducible Specht modules in arbitrary positive characteristic is a known open problem, and no general closed formula for the decomposition numbers of $S_n$ in a fixed positive characteristic is claimed anywhere on this page. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
before.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine, and record the boundary without asserting any unproved classification. Provenance: statement literature-derived, proof not-applicable; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.

after.title: General type-A decomposition numbers remain unsolved
after.statement:
The two preceding constraints on the decomposition matrix of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are real but limited, and neither solves the general problem.

(i) Dominance unitriangularity ([[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]) determines only the diagonal entries $d_{\mu\mu}=1$ and the vanishing region $d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$; it gives no value for an off-diagonal entry.

(ii) The q-Schaper/Jantzen sum formula ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]]) is an identity for the sum of the positive Jantzen filtration submodules. Its individual signed hook terms are not multiplicity bounds. After the whole virtual sum is expanded in simple classes and all cancellations are performed, its nonnegative simple coefficients bound the corresponding radical composition multiplicities from above; it neither determines a general multiplicity nor produces a positive combinatorial rule.

Special coefficient regimes and low-rank calculations determine additional entries (canonically based, weight-one, and small-$n$ cases), but the classification of irreducible Specht modules in arbitrary positive characteristic is a known open problem, and no general closed formula for the decomposition numbers of $S_n$ in a fixed positive characteristic is claimed anywhere on this page. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
after.strategy: Prose Remark; no argument phase or proof claim. Correct boundary: signed hook terms are not bounds; only complete simple-class positive-submodule coefficients bound radical multiplicity.
